predecessors.name: Kingdom of Thessalonica
predecessors.text: Boniface of Montferrat's rights to Crete, sold for silver marks, an annual revenue share and Venetian support for his Thessalonica ambitions

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: Chania 1645, Rethymno 1646, the rest of the island by 1648, Candia surrendered in September 1669 (infobox 'Successor: Ottoman Crete')

successors.name: Republic of Venice
successors.text: the isolated fortresses of Spinalonga, Gramvousa and Souda, which Venice kept at the 1669 peace along with Tinos and Kythera; the Ottomans took them in 1715

ledger.x: 1206: the Genoese Enrico Pescatore, Count of Malta, seizes Crete.
1648: the island is Ottoman except Candia.
1669: Venice loses Candia, and Crete with it.
1669: the Kingdom of Candia ends after 464 years.

wars.name: Genoese-Venetian war for Crete
wars.outcome: Enrico Pescatore took large parts of Crete from 1206; Venice failed in 1207, took Palaiokastro in 1209 and drove him out by 1212; a treaty of 11 May 1217 ended the war with Crete in Venetian hands.

wars.name: Revolt of Skordyles and Melissenos
wars.outcome: The Cretan rebels reached a treaty with Venice on 13 September 1219.

wars.name: Revolt of Alexios Kallergis
wars.outcome: The largest revolt to that date began in 1282 and ended with the Peace of Alexios Kallergis, signed on 28 April 1299.

wars.name: Revolt of Saint Titus
wars.outcome: The Venetian feudal lords rose on 9 August 1363 and declared the Republic of Saint Titus; a Venetian fleet arrived on 7 May 1364 and Candia surrendered on 9 May.

wars.name: Cretan War
wars.outcome: The Ottomans landed on 23 June 1645, took Canea (22 August 1645) and Rethymno (20 October 1646), held near-total possession of the island by 1648 and besieged Candia from May 1648 until it surrendered on 5 September 1669.

certainty.note: An island: the coast is the border.
The Ottoman-Venetian front in the Cretan War is not described district by district on any page opened; the fortress of Candia and the three island forts are points, not lines.
